senses.gloss:
doṣa
(‘that which contaminates’, defect)
------------------------------------------
Derived from the root ‘duṣ’ (‘to contaminate,’ ‘to spoil’) , the word ‘doṣa’ is used in several senses such as: fault, sin, vice, crime, disrespect, abuse, evil and deficiency.
However, it is used in a technical sense too, in certain fields of knowledge.
In literary compositions, दोष can be of five types, pertaining to the use of the word or a part of the word, sentence, meaning and sentiment. They are respectively known as padadoṣa, padāṁśadoṣa, vākyadoṣa, arthadoṣa and rasadoṣa. These defects are sometimes raised to ten or even more.
In तर्क or लोगिच्, the doṣas are broadly categorised as lakṣaṇadoṣa (defect in implicatory meaning) and hetudoṣa (defect in the enumeration of causes).
In the आयुर्वेद, the main constituents of health are the three doṣas or हुमोउर्स्: kapha (phlegm), vāta (wind) and pitta (bile). If they are in a balanced state, health will be maintained. If they are disturbed, disease results.
